The court allowed an exception for over 2,800 individuals with serious criminal antecedents. The central government sought this liberty while committing to honor assurances given to student representatives. The order follows the withdrawal of a planned march by the Cockroach Janta Party.
items.title: Supreme Court Quashes All FIRs Against NEET Protesters Across India

key_points: India has mapped over 28,000 glacial lakes in the Himalayas, with hundreds showing significant expansion since 1984.
The Central Water Commission monitors nearly 3,000 water bodies monthly, identifying many that require vigorous disaster monitoring.
The 2023 South Lhonak disaster highlighted how cascading hazards like landslides and permafrost thaw can trigger massive floods.
India has approved a Rs. 150-crore mitigation programme and is developing indigenous early-warning technologies for high-risk lakes.
Transboundary challenges persist as many hazardous lakes lie in Nepal or Tibet, complicating warning and response efforts.
items.summary: India is expanding its monitoring of Himalayan glacial lakes to manage the risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The National Remote Sensing Centre mapped over 28,000 lakes, finding that hundreds have expanded significantly since 1984. The Central Water Commission now monitors nearly 3,000 water bodies monthly, noting that many show increased water spread. Experts emphasize that risk depends on downstream exposure and slope stability, not just lake size. The catastrophic 2023 South Lhonak disaster in Sikkim demonstrated how cascading hazards like landslides and permafrost thaw can trigger massive floods. India has integrated risk assessments into a dynamic list of 195 high-risk lakes and approved a Rs. 150-crore mitigation programme. Agencies are also developing indigenous early-warning technologies and reviewing hydropower dam designs. However, transboundary challenges remain, as many hazardous lakes lie in Nepal or Tibet. Ultimately, effective warning systems must connect satellite observations to actionable decisions for communities downstream.
items.title: India monitors Himalayan glacial lakes to manage GLOF risks

items.summary: Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football on August 31, concluding a 21-year career with the Argentina national team. The 39-year-old forward stated that while the decision hurts deeply, he believes the time has come to step away from representing his country. His international career began in 2005 and ended after leading the team to victory in the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. Following the death of his father, Messi had previously expressed serious doubts about continuing to play professionally. He now joins Diego Maradona and Pelé as one of the greatest players in football history.

items.summary: The article argues that recent Himalayan floods were not natural acts but consequences of unheeded scientific warnings and dangerous development. The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) reports that glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalayas are melting at an accelerating rate, with ice loss doubling since 2000. Unregulated construction in river valleys and unstable slopes has created death traps, ignoring past disasters like the 2013 Kedarnath floods. A 2025 study found that 66 per cent of sampled hydropower projects lie on potential glacial lake outburst tracks. The author calls for strictly enforced construction restrictions, redesigned hydropower safety standards, and a trilateral monitoring agreement between India, China, and Nepal to prevent future catastrophes.
items.title: Nepal floods show Himalayan disasters stem from ignored warnings and reckless building

key_points: A building engineer from Tamil Nadu reportedly bought an acre of lunar land as a wedding gift for his future wife.
Private organizations sell these lunar plots as novelty deeds that confer no legal ownership under international space law.

items.summary: A building engineer from Tamil Nadu reportedly purchased an acre of lunar land as a wedding gift, illustrating the novelty nature of such sales. Private organizations sell these plots as commemorative certificates that confer no legal proprietorship under international agreements. The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 prohibits any country from claiming sovereignty over celestial bodies, meaning no government can validate private deeds to the Moon. While the United States has adopted laws allowing private ownership of extracted space resources, major powers like Russia and China have not ratified the Moon Agreement which declared lunar resources the common heritage of mankind. Consequently, buying a plot of land on the Moon remains a symbolic gesture rather than a legitimate real estate investment.
items.title: Engineer buys Moon land as gift, but international law blocks ownership

items.summary: Chockalingam Narayanan, Head of Equities at ICICI Prudential AMC, stated in an interview with Mint that investors should currently favor value over growth and prioritize current earnings. He noted that while foreign institutional investor selling reflects asset allocation rather than a rejection of India's structural story, the market now requires greater differentiation based on balance sheet strength. Narayanan advised that IT stocks are not outright contra bets, though their business models must adapt to AI before becoming bullish targets. He highlighted that commodity producers benefit from higher prices while consumers face margin pressure, making sectors like metals and auto ancillaries interesting. The expert emphasized that a cheap valuation alone is not a contrarian thesis without a foreseeable path to earnings recovery.
